simple.meaning: עָרַר (ʻârar) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to bare ; figuratively, to demolish.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Isaiah, Jeremiah, beginning at Isaiah 23:13. Its contexts include land, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָרַר (H6209).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: עָרַר (ʻârar) / H6209 is traced through Isaiah 23:13, Isaiah 32:11, Jeremiah 51:58 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Behold, the land of the Chaldeans. This people didn’t exist. The Assyrians founded it for those who dwell in the wilderness. They set up their towers. They overthrew its palaces. They made it a ruin.
